F-01.cause: New Netlify projects default to private visitor access.
F-01.fix: Production set to public; deploy previews kept private.
F-01.found: Every visitor got 401 Unauthorized and a login page.
F-01.retest: Live site returns 200 to anonymous visitors.
F-01.title: Live site hidden behind a Netlify login

F-02.cause: Netlify's "Powered by Netlify" badge injects inline code, which the site's security policy correctly blocks.
F-02.fix: Badge turned off (security policy kept strict).
F-02.found: 2 red Content-Security-Policy errors in the console on every page load.
F-02.retest: Zero console errors on the live site.
F-02.title: Console errors from an injected Netlify script

F-03.cause: It relied only on a CSS animation to hide itself.
F-03.fix: Two independent timer failsafes remove it after 1.6 s and 2.5 s.
F-03.found: In a full-page render the KS loading screen never cleared.
F-03.title: Loading screen could cover the whole page

F-04.cause: Count-up reset them to 0 and waited until they were 60% visible.
F-04.fix: Real numbers stay until the animation actually starts.
F-04.found: On desktop, the four stats at the bottom of the hero read 0+.
F-04.title: Stats showed "0+"

F-05.cause: The effect counted frames; browsers slow timers in background tabs.
F-05.fix: Timed by the clock so it always finishes on schedule.
F-05.found: Hero name read "KJBVJX" instead of KELVIN.
F-05.title: Name could stay scrambled

F-06.cause: One CV variant was missing a value in the build script.
F-06.fix: Value added, plus a build check that stops if any placeholder is left unfilled.
F-06.found: "Personal portfolio" link in the downloadable CV pointed to a placeholder.
F-06.retest: All CV links embedded and resolving.
F-06.title: Broken portfolio link in the public CV

F-07.found: Text extraction read headings as "P R O F I L E".
F-07.retest: Headings extract as PROFILE, EXPERIENCE, etc.
F-07.title: CV headings unreadable to screening software

F-08.cause: A CSS display rule overrode the hidden attribute.
F-08.fix: Global rule so hidden always hides.
F-08.found: Every test case's details showed on load.
F-08.title: QA Lab test details all expanded

F-09.fix: Buttons no longer shrink or wrap; brand text hidden under 400px.
F-09.found: "Auto · dark" broke onto two lines when the menu was open at 375px.
F-09.title: Theme button wrapped on narrow phones

F-10.cause: Horizontal overflow container also allowed vertical overflow.
F-10.found: A vertical scrollbar indicator next to the tabs on desktop.
F-10.title: Stray scrollbar beside case study tabs

F-11.found: Numbers had 7 digits after +233 instead of 9 (own and a referee's).
F-11.retest: Private CV numbers tap to call and open WhatsApp.
F-11.title: Phone numbers on the old CV were incomplete

F-12.cause: LinkedIn and WhatsApp need full addresses for previews.
F-12.fix: Absolute image URL, og:url and canonical link added after the site got its final address.
F-12.found: Share image and page URL were relative paths.
F-12.title: Share preview image would not show

F-13.cause: Brand text, the labelled theme button and the Menu button did not fit on one line once text scaled up; '/ portfolio' was only hidden below 400px.
F-13.fix: Under 520px the theme button becomes icon-only (full name kept for screen readers) and '/ portfolio' is hidden.
F-13.found: With the phone font size increased (130%), the header on ~412px-wide phones (Galaxy A15, A32) overflowed: the Menu button ended at 432px on a 412px screen, so it could not be tapped. Also failed on 320px screens.
F-13.retest: Deployed and retested on the live site at 320, 360 and 412px with 130% and 150% text: Menu fully on screen every time. TC-36 now passes on Galaxy A15 and A32 (emulated); regression run on S22, iPhone 13 and A15 found no new failures. Confirmed by Kelvin on a real Galaxy A32 with the system font at maximum.
F-13.title: Menu button pushed off-screen with large text

F-14.title: Scroll fade-in timing different on the test report page
F-14.found: Comparing the homepage and the test report on laptop and phone, the fade-in on the report felt later and inconsistent. Measured: a ~500px element with its top 20% into the screen had started fading on the homepage but not on the report.
F-14.cause: The report's helper used 'threshold || 0.2'. In JavaScript 0 counts as empty, so the intended threshold of 0 became 0.2 and tall elements (device table, issue cards) waited until 20% of their height was visible.
F-14.fix: Only fall back to 0.2 when no threshold is given, so 0 is respected.
F-14.retest: Same measurement on the live site: the report's device table now starts fading at the same point as on the homepage. Zero console errors.
F-14.foundBy: Kelvin (visual comparison across pages and devices)
